topic: 100 Years of NASA & American Rocket Evolution (1926–2026) — From Goddard's Naked Metal Pipes & Vanguard's Pencil Collapse to Saturn V F-1 Nozzles, Shuttle Shock Diamonds & Artemis SLS

factual_references.citation: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum — March 16, 1926: Dr. Robert H. Goddard's First Liquid-Propellant Rocket Flight ('Nell', Auburn, Massachusetts).
factual_references.supported_claims: Goddard's 1926 liquid oxygen/gasoline rocket lacked an aerodynamic fuselage or nose cone, placing the combustion chamber and nozzle at the top above naked fuel lines and suspended tanks.

factual_references.citation: NASA History Division — Vanguard TV-3 Launch Failure (Dec 6, 1957), Juno I / Explorer 1 Spinning Solid-Rocket Cluster (Jan 31, 1958), and Mercury-Atlas Pressurized Stainless-Steel Balloon Tanks (1962).
factual_references.supported_claims: Vanguard TV-3 rose ~4 feet before collapsing into flames; Juno I spun an upper-stage tub of 11 scaled-down Sergeant rockets; Atlas used <1 mm pressurized stainless-steel balloon tanks and 1.5-stage side booster staging.

factual_references.citation: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center & Kennedy Space Center — Saturn IB (8 Redstone/Jupiter tanks & 8 H-1 engines), Saturn V (363 ft, five F-1 engines at 7.5M lbf), Space Shuttle RS-25, and Artemis Space Launch System (four RS-25s + twin SRBs at 8.8M lbf).
factual_references.supported_claims: Saturn IB clustered eight narrow tanks over eight H-1 engines; Saturn V stood 36 stories with five 3.7 m F-1 nozzles generating 7.5M lbf; Space Shuttle paired a ceramic-tiled orbiter with an external tank and 3 RS-25s; Artemis SLS generates 8.8M lbf while propellant remains ~88–90% of launch mass.

shot_list.story_beat: March 16, 1926 Goddard rocket 'Nell' in 4K archival detail
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Direct, unmistakable 4K archival photograph of the exact March 16, 1926 machine as the narrator tells viewers to look closely.

shot_list.story_beat: Animated schematic of missing nose cone and missing outer skin
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Clarifies the counterintuitive inverted geometry of Goddard's skinless 1926 rocket in 2.55 seconds.

shot_list.story_beat: Laboratory close-up of Goddard's top nozzle, naked metal pipes, and dual fuel tanks
shot_list.editorial_rationale: High-resolution NASA archival laboratory photograph proving the exact top-nozzle + naked-pipes + lower-tanks architecture.

shot_list.story_beat: Late-1950s fragile metal-pencil orbital rocket
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Direct visual match to 'fragile metal pencils'.

shot_list.story_beat: 1957 Vanguard pencil rocket collapsing into flames
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Timed so the pad explosion erupts right as the narrator says 'collapsing into flames'.

shot_list.story_beat: 1958 JPL engineers assembling Juno I miniature rocket tubes
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Hands-on 1958 JPL assembly footage proving how small and exposed America's first orbital upper-stage rockets were.

shot_list.story_beat: 1962 Mercury-Atlas stainless-steel balloon-tank liftoff
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Direct visual match to 'gleamed like solid steel' while explaining the dime-thin pressurized balloon tank.

shot_list.story_beat: Thin-walled cylindrical rocket tank structure
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Visualizes lightweight cylindrical tank walls inside NASA's vertical bay.

shot_list.story_beat: Mercury-Atlas mid-sky ascent
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Tracks Atlas climbing steeply mid-sky.

shot_list.story_beat: Exposed mid-1960s rocket engine struts and raw plumbing
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Literal close-up of wide-open mid-sixties rocket machinery and steel struts.

shot_list.story_beat: 1965 Gemini Titan II twin-engine HD launch
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Authentic NASA HD Resource Reel scan of Gemini Titan II firing twin engines at Pad 19.

shot_list.story_beat: 1966 Saturn IB eight clustered missile tanks
shot_list.editorial_rationale: 1:1 literal visual proof of the 8 clustered missile tanks described in the narration.

shot_list.story_beat: 1969 Saturn V 36-story colossus hull sweep
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Sweeps vertically down the actual 36-story Saturn V hull before diving beneath its five F-1 nozzles in S14.

shot_list.story_beat: Five cavernous 4-meter F-1 nozzles beside NASA technician
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Real human technician beside the five F-1 bells makes 'nearly four meters wide' viscerally undeniable.

shot_list.story_beat: Apollo 11 500-fps F-1 ignition and cascading cryogenic ice
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Historic Apollo 11 500-fps Camera E-8 footage matches 'silver batting', 'thrust', and 'ice cascaded' simultaneously.

shot_list.story_beat: Space Shuttle asymmetric ceramic glider and orange tank climb
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Shows the side-mounted winged ceramic-tiled glider + orange external tank rolling skyward.

shot_list.story_beat: RS-25 hydrogen engine firing with glowing shock column
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Direct close-up NASA Stennis static-fire footage of the RS-25 hydrogen exhaust plume.

shot_list.story_beat: Colossal rocket propellant static test burn (~90% propellant mass fraction)
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Visualizes the staggering propellant burn rate imposed by the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation.

shot_list.story_beat: 4K close-up beneath Artemis SLS's four upgraded RS-25 engines
shot_list.editorial_rationale: 4K KSC hardware close-up showing a century of engine evolution from 1926's tiny pipe nozzle to four RS-25 bells.

shot_list.story_beat: Artemis I SLS 8.8-million-pound night liftoff toward the Moon
shot_list.editorial_rationale: Unforgettable 100-year visual payoff contrasting 8.8M-lbf Artemis liftoff back into Frame 0's tiny 1926 pipe rocket.
